subject: Warning messages in the SEM function in Lavaan

messages.author: b48ebf16ed4cffef
messages.subject: Warning messages in the SEM function in Lavaan
parts:
Hello, I'm new to using lavaan. Before using it, I used SPSS to build model structural equations. Currently, I'm trying to get the covariances between all my exogenous variables, as in the SPSS, but I'm getting the following warning messages:

1: In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, cluster = cluster,  :
  lavaan WARNING: some observed variances are (at least) a factor 1000 times larger than others; use varTable(fit) to investigate
2: In lavaan::lavaan(model = model.01, data = rich.byweb, estimator = "MLM",  :
  lavaan WARNING: syntax contains parameters involving exogenous covariates; switching to fixed.x = FALSE

I was wondering if these warnings were impacting my results? How can I solve this problem? Thank you.

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Warning messages in the SEM function in Lavaan
parts:
Vinicius,
1: Your data is not properly scaled for SEM analysis.  You need to rescale some of the variables by multiplying by powers of 10 to give the variances the same order of magnitude.  See Rex Kline's SEM book for a more detailed explanation (or whatever book you have handy).

2: Suppose that you had a model with a lot of exogenous variables that are all freely correlated.  This can overwhelm the chi-square goodness of fit statistic.  So, the default setting of fixed.x = TRUE can help make the goodness of fit test more informative by excluding variances and covariances of exogenous variables.  You can shut this off by including fixed.x = FALSE as a parameter to the function that you use to fit your model.  However, if all you want to do is see the covariances, you can use lavInspect(myFit, what='sampstat') while leaving fixed.x TRUE.  This is only an issue if you have observed causal variables in your model (e.g., path analysis, MIMIC models, etc.).  If all the observed variables are indicators of latent variables, then none are exogenous in the relevant sense.

Keith
